findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define exactly which added-line patterns count as a 'new conditional branch' and add a replay/unit fixture whose ONLY src addition is such a branch (no def/class), asserting SELECT.
evidence: Step 2: 'starts a function/method/class definition or a new conditional branch'
AC2 replay cases: d9e0f0e733 '15 added definitions', 721cb7d6ac 'moved definitions', 1c2bf6e57b 'module split' — all def/class; negatives are comment-only and annotation-only
No AC exercises a diff whose sole src addition is a new conditional branch with no def/class
'0 added branch lines' is mentioned only for the 1547 negative
findings.finding: Step 2 says the detector fires when an added `src/**` line 'starts a function/method/class definition OR a new conditional branch', but no acceptance criterion or cited-corpus fixture exercises the branch-only trigger path, and 'new conditional branch' is never defined (which token patterns count — `if`/`elif`/`for`/`while`/`except`/`case`/boolean guards?).
findings.location: Approach step 2; Acceptance Criteria (all replay cases are def/class shapes)
scenarios: A change adding an `if`/`except` branch to existing product logic with no new def and no test file — the plan claims it triggers, but nothing proves it and the executor must guess what a 'branch' is
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the branch keywords the detector matches (e.g. leading `if `/`elif `/`for `/`while `/`except`/`case ` on an added line under a src header) and add an AC parametrisation case 'branch-only src addition → SELECT'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact prompt wording for the guard (vii) narrowing: define, in reviewer-applicable terms, how the LLM distinguishes 'newly introduced behaviour' from 'pre-existing code' and what qualifies as 'a named violating input', OR wire the deterministic trigger provenance into the reviewer's prompt context so the distinction need not be re-derived.
evidence: Plan step 5: 'Narrow guard (vii) ... so a gap on *newly introduced* behaviour with a named violating input is blocking-eligible, while a gap on pre-existing code stays advisory.'
code-review-tests.md:97 current guard (vii): 'bare coverage-gap demands ("no test for X") without a concrete failure path — not blocking' — a prompt-side flag/no-flag rule the LLM applies.

workflow_ops.py:61-65 returns only context/changed_files/scope_context to the reviewer; _has_added_definition is computed in registry.content_triggered_overlays (workflow_ops.py:99) for SELECTION, so the trigger provenance is not visible to the prompt.

ABSENCE: the plan specifies no prompt wording defining 'newly introduced', 'pre-existing', or 'a named violating input' as reviewer-applicable criteria; search for 'newly introduced' / 'blocking-eligible' in reviewers/ returns no existing vocabulary to reuse.
findings.finding: Step 5 adds a new LLM decision rule to guard (vii) — 'a gap on newly introduced behaviour with a named violating input is blocking-eligible, while a gap on pre-existing code stays advisory' — but does not define, for the reviewer prompt, how the LLM determines 'newly introduced' vs 'pre-existing' or what constitutes 'a named violating input'. The deterministic _has_added_definition signal that encodes this in registry.py is used only for overlay SELECTION and is not passed into the reviewer's prompt context (workflow_ops.py:61-65 supplies context/changed_files/scope_context, no trigger reason), so the prompt LLM must re-derive the distinction unaided from vocabulary the plan leaves unspecified.
scenarios: A src refactor that renames an existing function (delete+add) surfaces as an added definition; the reviewer must decide whether the behaviour is 'newly introduced' or 'pre-existing' with no defined rule, risking inconsistent blocking eligibility.

A reviewer sees a coverage gap on a def added in the diff but cannot tell whether it is genuinely new behaviour vs a moved/pre-existing definition (the diff has no -M rename info per Approach step 3), so the newly-introduced/pre-existing split becomes a coin-flip.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either drop 'or a new conditional branch' from the `_has_added_definition` scope (definitions are what all cited corpus cases require), or add a replay case + acceptance-criterion input that exercises branch-line triggering so the added scope is grounded in a done-definition.
evidence: Step 2: fires when an added line under src/** 'starts a function/method/class definition or a new conditional branch'
AC replay set is definition-keyed: '15 added definitions', 'moved definitions, 3', 'module split, 22'; NOT-SELECT cases are comment-only (1547) and annotation-only signature rewrite (1703)

No AC or Testing entry names a branch-line input; existing _REMOVED_DECL_RE (registry.py:399-412) covers only def/class/function signatures, so branch detection is genuinely new logic added without a corpus case behind it
ANTI-FP note: this is not NIH — the added-definition half legitimately extends the _has_removed_declaration family; the finding is narrowly the unexercised branch-detection scope
findings.finding: The detector's 'or a new conditional branch' clause adds scope not driven by any cited corpus case or acceptance criterion — all three SELECT cases (388/1920/1737) and both NOT-SELECT cases (1547/1703) are about added/annotation-only DEFINITIONS, not branch lines; no AC or parametrised-replay shape exercises branch detection.
findings.location: Approach step 2 ('starts a function/method/class definition or a new conditional branch') vs Acceptance Criteria (all cases definition/comment/annotation shaped)
scenarios: A future maintainer implements branch-line regex and cannot regression-test it against the corpus, or it silently over-fires on ordinary refactors that add an if/for
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the v1 detector to added def/method/class declarations only (matching the existing _REMOVED_DECL_PATTERNS applied to `+` lines), and defer branch-line detection to a follow-up with its own corpus case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the `_has_added_definition` content trigger is Python-specific (matches `def`/`class` under `src/**`) and either scope it explicitly to Python targets or record that non-Python targets fall back to glob-only triggering.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'starts a function/method/class definition or a new conditional branch, AND no changed file matches the `tests` globs' — definition detection is Python `def`/`class`-shaped, confirmed by AC2's grep `^\+\s*(async +)?(def|class) `
Support matrix Target project: Ruby, Python, Java, Next.js, .NET, Terraform
Java/.NET add methods with `public`/`void`/`func` etc. and often under `main/`, not `def`/`class` under `src/`
findings.finding: The new content trigger `_has_added_definition` detects added behaviour by matching Python `(async +)?(def|class)` lines under a `src/**` path, but the code_review overlays run against arbitrary target projects (Ruby, Java, Next.js, .NET, Terraform). For a non-Python target, an added method/class does not match this syntax and may not live under `src/`, so the content trigger silently never fires — the plan presents the improvement without scoping it to Python targets or stating this language-specificity.
findings.location: Approach step 2 and Acceptance Criteria line 2 (`grep -cE '^\+\s*(async +)?(def|class) '`)
scenarios: Target project = Java in a monorepo: a change adds a new `public void foo()` method under `src/main/java/...` with no test file; the content trigger's `def|class`/`src/**` match yields no hit, the tests overlay is not selected, and the new-behaviour-with-no-test case the epic targets ships un-reviewed — the exact gap the plan set out to close is invisible for non-Python targets.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope note in Approach step 2 that the detector targets Python-shaped definitions and that non-Python target projects retain the existing glob-only trigger behaviour (accepted, not a regression).

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
